actors.scope: all six compose_replay_tape arguments are potentially adversarial from the function's own point of view even though the intended caller is a trusted test: record/session/published/consumer_document_sha256 could be a forged or cross-capture-mismatched tuple (row 3, row 10); roster_relative_path could name a member outside the intended roster; raw_event_members could contain malformed metadata, wrong relative_paths, or be empty (row 5, row 9); the roster and raw-event BYTES resolved via read_member_bytes are untrusted regardless of caller intent, exactly as verify_causal_order already treats ordered_envelope_bytes as untrusted (evidence 0187's own framing, still true here one layer up)

authority_boundary_statement: compose_replay_tape crosses no NEW trust boundary: every credential it touches (record, session, published) was already minted by a real authorize_capture_set call before compose_replay_tape is invoked, and every read it performs (roster bytes, raw-event bytes) goes back through ADR-0129's own already-verified accessor, which independently rebinds record/session/published/consumer_document_sha256/relative_path and rechecks sealed member digests on every call. compose_replay_tape's own contribution to the trust boundary is entirely DOWNSTREAM validation: it must not silently accept a resolved-but-malformed roster or raw-event member, must not let a caller inject data_capture_root, and must genuinely re-verify via the build/canonical_bytes/parse/verify_causal_order round trip rather than trusting its own in-memory construction. This is consistent with ADR-0130/0141-0144's disjoint 'may this document CAPTURE this root' vs. 'are these envelope bytes in causal order' framing, now extended one hop further: 'was this specific record/session/published triple ACTUALLY the one that captured this content, and does the content it names actually verify end-to-end.'

class_function_inventory.name: compose_replay_tape(record, session, published, consumer_document_sha256, roster_relative_path, raw_event_members)
class_function_inventory.pin: the exact 10-step body ADR-0146 Decision point 7 specifies, verbatim: (1) stream = published.sealed.prepared.stream_id; (2) roster_bytes = record.read_member_bytes(session, published, consumer_document_sha256, roster_relative_path); (3) parse+validate via _check_composed_tape_roster_fixture, raising ProductionError naming every problem; (4) source_rank_policy_sha256 = sha256(roster_bytes).hexdigest(); (5) source_rank_by_id built from the validated roster; (6) for each entry in raw_event_members IN ORDER (no sorting performed by this function): (6a) raw_bytes = record.read_member_bytes(...), (6b) parse+validate via _check_raw_event_member, (6c) source_rank = source_rank_by_id[source_id] with an absent source_id accumulated into the raised error rather than a bare KeyError, (6d) assemble the 15-field event-envelope/v2 object, (6e) validate via _check_event_envelope (the SAME function verify_causal_order itself uses per-position), (6f) envelope_bytes = _canonical_bytes(envelope); append to ordered_envelope_bytes and hashlib.sha256(envelope_bytes).hexdigest() to ordered_envelope_digests; (7) data_capture_root computed from the live published token INSIDE this function, never an argument; (8) data_captured_receipt = record.lifecycle_captured_receipt_sha256(stream, consumer_document_sha256); (9) tape = CapturedReplayTape._build(...), reparsed = CapturedReplayTape.parse(tape.canonical_bytes()); (10) verify_causal_order(reparsed, ordered_envelope_bytes) -- on success returns reparsed, on failure the ProductionError propagates unedited, no second error-handling layer

class_function_inventory.name: data_capture_root derivation (Decision point 4's own named open pin -- THIS Phase 0 matrix resolves it)
class_function_inventory.pin: data_capture_root = _canonical_hash(published.descriptor). NOT sealed._member_manifest_sha256 ('the F4 publication receipt's own self digest' option the ADR text names as the alternative): that attribute is underscore-prefixed on trust.py's private _Sealed class, and reading it from bundles.py would violate the exact underscore-prefix/no-private-cross-package-reach rule AGENTS.md states twice and tests/production/test_purity.py's test_no_private_name_is_imported_from_another_package machine-checks (code_read above). published.descriptor is the ONE public, non-underscore, already-frozen attribute _Published exposes that identifies the captured root (root_ref, snapshot_version, document_sha256, node, output, purpose) -- exactly the shape Decision point 7's own reasoning requires ('calls only their existing public methods/attributes'). This is a code-shape-level argument (mirrors evidence 0187 row 9's reasoning), not merely a preference, and Phase 0 pins it as the required implementation choice, closing the ADR's own 'remains the Phase 0 pin' deferral.

class_function_inventory.name: data_capture_root tamper-resistance (task item 6)
class_function_inventory.pin: a caller cannot substitute a different root because (a) data_capture_root is not a parameter at all -- it is computed from published.descriptor inside the function, and (b) published itself is independently rebound against the exact committed record/session/descriptor on EVERY read_member_bytes call (steps 2 and 6a, which both run BEFORE step 7). A published token whose descriptor was tampered, or that belongs to a different capture than record/session, fails read_member_bytes's own 'P4 record/session/publication mismatch' or 'P4 sealed member manifest mismatch' refusal at step 2, before compose_replay_tape ever reaches step 7 -- so a successful tape can only ever be built from a published token that already survived the SAME binding check twice.

class_function_inventory.name: _check_composed_tape_roster_fixture(value)

entry_points: compose_replay_tape, full success path, steps 1-10, driven via f4._publish/authorize_capture_set on the ordinary fixed CapturedAuthorizationAuthority

matrix.forbidden_effect: any F4/broker/signer/ledger call other than the two accessor methods; any silent success despite a malformed fixture; a second call succeeding by re-reading already-consumed member bytes

cases: identical fixture shape to row 1, but record/session/published are produced by authorize_capture_set on the DYNAMIC authority (trust._DynamicP4TrustedArtifactResolver / _DynamicCapturedAuthorizationContract) rather than the fixed one -- this is the ADR's OWN stated positive proof case (Decision point 2), not a substitutable variant of row 1

matrix.family: task item (3) -- forged/mismatched record/session/published triple not corresponding to a real committed CAPTURED admission
entry_points: compose_replay_tape step 1 (published.sealed.prepared.stream_id) and step 2 (record.read_member_bytes) -- the FIRST accessor call in the function body
cases: record is a genuine CapturedAuthorizationRecord from a DIFFERENT, valid, unrelated capture (not this stream/consumer_document_sha256) -- p4_receipt_digest/read_p4_member's own _p4_record_capture lookup fails to find an entry
session is a genuine LaunchSession but from a DIFFERENT capture than record (session is entry[5] identity check fails)

published is a genuine _Published token but for a different root than the one record/session captured (descriptor mismatch at the request['captures'][index][3]==dict(descriptor) check)
consumer_document_sha256 is a syntactically valid sha256-shaped string that simply does not match the frozen document actually used at capture time
matrix.expected_outcome: compose_replay_tape raises (ProductionError from its own accumulate-then-raise style is NOT required here -- read_member_bytes/lifecycle_captured_receipt_sha256 raise ValueError directly per their own docstring's Raises section; Phase 0 should pin whether compose_replay_tape lets that ValueError propagate unwrapped or wraps it into ProductionError -- ADR text does not say, and this is a genuine remaining Phase 0 pin for the independent skeptic, since Decision point 10's own text only discusses ProductionError propagation for verify_causal_order's raise at step 10, not the earlier accessor-raised ValueError at steps 2/6a/8)
matrix.forbidden_effect: compose_replay_tape ever returning a CapturedReplayTape built from member bytes that were not genuinely authorized by THIS exact record/session/published/consumer_document_sha256 combination

cases: schema_version is a near-miss string (e.g. 'dskit.composed-tape-roster-fixture/v2' or missing the /v1 suffix)
sources is missing, not a list, or an empty list
one source item missing source_id or rank, or with an extra unknown key
source_id present but empty string, or non-string (int/None)
two sources share the same source_id

rank values skip a value (0,1,3) or duplicate a value (0,1,1)
rank values start above zero (1,2,3 instead of 0,1,2)

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.finding: the exception type compose_replay_tape should let propagate from steps 2/6a/8's accessor calls is not pinned by the ADR text
open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.detail: record.read_member_bytes and record.lifecycle_captured_receipt_sha256 raise ValueError per their own docstrings (trust.py:4824-4898), while compose_replay_tape's own content-validation steps (3, 6b, 6e) and verify_causal_order (step 10) raise ProductionError. ADR-0146 Decision point 7's prose never states whether compose_replay_tape wraps an accessor-raised ValueError into a ProductionError or lets it propagate unwrapped as a ValueError. Both are internally consistent with different parts of the ADR text (Decision point 10's last bullet only discusses verify_causal_order's own raise); this Phase 0 matrix recommends the independent skeptic pin one explicitly before RED, since RED's exact assertion (pytest.raises(ProductionError) vs pytest.raises(ValueError) vs pytest.raises((ProductionError, ValueError))) depends on it.

Recommend RED add a small dedicated regression test (or the independent skeptic explicitly accept documentation-only enforcement as sufficient for a deployment_eligible=false slice).

Recommend Phase 0 pin default-deny for consistency with _check_tape/_check_event_envelope/_check_composed_tape_roster_fixture/_check_raw_event_member's own accumulate-then-raise style, even though raw_event_members entries are plain caller-supplied dicts rather than resolved-and-parsed bytes.

open_findings_for_independent_skeptic.detail: ADR-0146 Decision point 4/7 explicitly states 'the exact bytes hashed... remains the Phase 0 pin.' This matrix pins it (class_function_inventory above) using a code-shape-level argument (the underscore-prefix API-contract rule, machine-checked by test_purity.py's test_no_private_name_is_imported_from_another_package, forecloses the alternative). The independent skeptic should specifically re-verify this reasoning rather than accept it on the implementer's authority alone, since it is the single highest-leverage design choice this matrix makes that the ADR itself declined to make.
